title: Deciding How Much the AI Should Do
intro: Autonomy is a product decision. Grant the lowest level that delivers the outcome.

topics.title: Deciding How Much the AI Should Do

learn.title: Five autonomy levels
learn.text:
**1 · Suggest** — AI advises; you act
**2 · Draft** — AI starts; you finish
**3 · Confirm** — AI proposes; you approve
**4 · Bounded** — AI acts within hard limits
**5 · Monitor** — AI runs; you watch

Judge by impact, reversibility, reliability, sensitivity, and whether anyone would notice a bad outcome.

**Reversibility and detectability set the ceiling:** hard-to-undo or hard-to-spot actions get lower autonomy, however reliable the model.

try.q: An action is reliable but hard to undo and hard to notice. What autonomy level?
try.explain: Reversibility and detectability set the ceiling regardless of reliability.

learn.title: Trust is calibrated, not maximised
learn.text:
**T.R.U.S.T.**, applied at the moment someone decides whether to rely on the output:

• **Truthful expectations** — say what the AI does and doesn't do, in task terms
• **Reasons and provenance** — claim-level citations; why this recommendation
• **Uncertainty and limits** — plain-language ranges, not an unexplained “78%”
• **Safeguards and control** — inspect → adjust → correct
• **Track record** — let people see how it has performed

The goal isn't maximum trust. It's trust that matches how reliable the system actually is.

try.q: What is wrong with showing an unexplained “78% confident”?
options: A number without meaning doesn't calibrate trust
Percentages always imply a false level of precision
try.explain: Plain-language ranges tell people what to do with it.

learn.title: The anatomy of a chat turn
learn.text:
**C.O.N.V.E.R.S.E.** covers what a single AI turn needs: context carried in, options offered, a visible next step, an escape route, and a way to correct the system.

The practical test: after one turn, can the user tell what the AI did, what it used, how sure it is, and what to do next?

try.q: What is the practical test for a single AI turn?
options: Can the user tell what it did and what to do next
Does it respond within the expected two-second window
Does it use the brand voice
try.explain: What it did, what it used, how sure it is, what comes next.

options: Whichever autonomy preference the user has selected in their settings
test.explain: Grant the lowest level that still delivers the outcome.

test.q: At which level does the AI act within hard limits?

options: Each claim shows where it came from
Links to the model's underlying training data
test.explain: Provenance attached to the claim, not the whole answer.

test.q: What is the goal of trust scaffolding?
options: Eliminating user scepticism about the output

test.q: What should safeguards let a user do?
test.explain: Control at the point of reliance.
